picks.excerpt: A look at the software now shaping which books get flagged, including BookLens, an AI-powered book-rating tool that 'hallucinates' and fabricates content details for titles that sometimes don't even exist. A cautionary case study in how unreliable generative-AI book analysis is being wired into discovery, rating and gatekeeping decisions across schools and libraries.
picks.rationale: Names a specific AI book-rating tool (BookLens) and its hallucination failure mode being wired into real gatekeeping — the most actionable design x AI story in the pool for anyone building or trusting AI book-analysis tools.

picks.excerpt: When NYT journalist Kashmir Hill found an AI-generated biography of herself for sale on Amazon, she bought and read it, then tried to trace its author, exposing how machine-written nonfiction is quietly filling retail catalogs. A pointed look at AI-authored books and the collapse of authorship signals for readers.
picks.rationale: Concrete, traceable case of AI-generated nonfiction flooding Amazon under a real person's name — actionable for authors, editors and readers weighing authorship trust.

picks.excerpt: As AI assistants increasingly mediate how research is discovered and read, this essay argues open science must shift focus from mere access to trust, interpretation and effective communication. It reframes what publishers and libraries owe readers when a machine, not a person, is doing the reading.
picks.rationale: Reframes scholarly publishing strategy for an AI-mediated reading layer — moves the goalpost from access to trust and interpretation, a distinct angle from prior disclosure-standard coverage.
